newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on mild export optimism.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on mild export optimism.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher on slight export optimism, but traders said thin volumes and a lack of selling really explained the market's price action Tuesday.
"It's really been the same story all day. We got off to a stronger start than expected and then basically held firm all day," a KCBT trader said.
Traders cited talk that Turkey bought 150,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat and 50,000 tonnes of U.S. white wheat.
"That Turkey (rumor) capped any possible rallies in here," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled two to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 3-1/2 cents at $4.52. March gained 2-1/4 cents to close at $3.98-1/2.
Some support came on talk that analytical firm Sparks Companies cut its estimate of 1997 U.S. winter wheat acreage by two million acres.
But the rumor appeared to contradict Monday's bearish comments by Sparks CEO Carrol Brunthaver, who said CBOT July wheat would be trading between $2.60 and $2.70 during harvest next summer.

Traders said Refco helped spark early buying when it bull-spread 400,000 Dec/March at 53 cents early and 500,000 March/May at 35 cents. E D & F Man bull-spread 600,000 March/May at 35 cents. CIS sold one million March.
